page.layout: One column of index entries, running down the page, with page numbers on their own indented lines between some entries.; One column of index entries, right part of the page: fragments of headwords at the left edge, page-number references at the right. Heading line "I N [?]" at the top.; One column of index entries, with page numbers after some entries, running from top to bottom. Above the column, a letter-spaced heading. Left of the column, partial marks from the neighbouring page edge.; One narrow strip: index words cut at the left edge, page references in a column at the right, aligned to the words.
page.notes: Right-hand edge of every line is cut off, so many entries end in partial words; those ends are left as far as they are visible. Several letters are faint and marked [?]. Long s is rendered as plain s. Left-edge headwords are fragments; they are copied as far as they are visible. Long s in the headwords is read as s. Several entries have no visible headword in this strip. The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of many entries; the visible letters are copied and the cut ones are marked [?]. Long s is printed as f in several words (e.g. "fervare", "fexaginti", "fibilare", "fighum"); written here as s. The readings "signum", "similem" and "simia" are uncertain. Partial marks at the left edge belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. No page number or running head is printed in this part. The strip is cut at the left, so the word beginnings are fragments and are kept as they stand. The reading "similiter" is inferred from the long-s form, which looks like "fimiliter" in the scan. Some left fragments (es, ó, n, t, im, go) could not be checked against a full word.
